sections_in_order: Description and Application of the Guidelines
General Clinical Guideline (framework, simultaneous ordering, repeat diagnostic, repeat therapeutic)

criteria_location: Clinical Indications, pp. 8-10 of 12. A generic 'General Clinical Guideline' (pp. 4-5) states cross-cutting rules (net benefit, peer-to-peer, repeat therapeutic intervention). Definitions on p.7 are needed by the criteria.
procedures_covered: Substernal ICD codes listed (0571T-0574T) but no substernal criteria

logic.top_level: pathways (about 20 any-of scenarios under one global survival condition; S-ICD an ALL list)

k_of_n.quote: Transvenous ICD placement is considered medically necessary in ANY of the following scenarios when survival with good functional status for more than one year is anticipated
Ischemic cardiomyopathy when ANY of the following apply
Lamin A/C cardiomyopathy with EITHER ... At least 2 of the following apply: LVEF < 45%; Non-sustained ventricular tachycardia; Male sex
At least ONE of the following applies: Inability to secure venous access; Immunocompromised individual; recurrent infections; Individual with endocarditis; younger age ... <= 21
following 90 days of GDMT, BOTH of the following are still present: LVEF <= 35%; NYHA functional class II or III

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: No exclusion list. Negative conditions are written into criteria: S-ICD requires the person 'does not require pacing for bradycardia ...' and 'does not have incessant ventricular tachycardia'. The global condition 'survival with good functional status for more than one year' acts as a prognosis exclusion.
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Device replacement is one scenario: 'Generator end-of-life criteria are present' OR 'The generator pocket needs to be opened for another reason ... AND the device is within 3 years of reaching end-of-life criteria'. The General Clinical Guideline repeat-therapeutic-intervention paragraph also applies.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy in an individual <= 70 years of age, when, following 90 days of GDMT, BOTH of the following are still present
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Compared with BCBSM's copy, which adds 'or otherwise supported by clinical scenario', Carelon makes 70 a hard limit (revision 07/2023 'added age limit').

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Subcutaneous device is preferred due to younger age of patient Individual is <= 21 years of age
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Two clauses run together in one bullet (the History says 04/15/2024 'replaced specific patient age with the broader term younger', but the stale '<= 21' text remains) so it is unclear whether 'younger' means <= 21 or is a judgment.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Syncope which is otherwise unexplained in an individual with structural heart disease
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: 'Structural heart disease' is defined in Definitions as LVEF < 50%, prior MI, valve disease, congenital; the criterion works only with that outside definition.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Abnormal blood pressure response to exercise or spontaneous nonsustained ventricular tachycardia in an individual who has ANY of the following
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: A bullet nested under hypertrophic cardiomyopathy by position but written as a stand-alone scenario with no diagnosis named; reader must infer the HCM context.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Syncope within the preceding 6 months suspected by clinical history to be arrhythmic
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Appears alongside another bullet 'Unexplained syncope within the preceding 6 months' with different qualifiers; overlapping HCM items.

requirement_kinds.quote: when survival with good functional status for more than one year is anticipated

Established diagnosis of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy / arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia / long QT / short QT / Brugada / cardiac sarcoidosis ... Phospholamban / FLNC / Lamin A/C cardiomyopathy
LVEF is <= 30% due to myocardial infarction >= 40 days previously in an individual with NYHA functional class I despite GDMT, who is at least 90 days post revascularization
Nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy in an individual <= 70 years of age
Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) comprising 15% of LV mass in a patient aged 19 years or older
positive electrophysiology study performed >= 96 hours following myocardial infarction
at least 90 days post revascularization (if revascularization has been performed)
An outpatient who has met criteria for, and is awaiting, heart transplant or ventricular assist device and who is NYHA functional class IV
The individual does not require pacing for bradycardia, overdrive pacing for termination of ventricular tachycardia, or cardiac resynchronization

Providers may be required to submit clinical documentation in support of a request for services. Such documentation must a) accurately reflect the clinical situation at the time of the requested service, and b) sufficiently document the ordering provider's clinical intent.

the device is within 3 years of reaching end-of-life criteria

codes.codes_tied_to_criteria: A CPT/HCPCS list (33215-33273, 93640, 93641, 00534, C1721-C1899) and a 'Substernal Implantable Defibrillators' list (0571T-0574T). No mapping to criteria; the substernal codes have no clinical indication section. 'Authorization requirements will vary by health plan.'

external_dependencies.what: Health plan policy may replace the guideline

in the case of reviews for Medicare Advantage Plans, the Guidelines are only applied where there are not fully established CMS criteria
the determination of appropriateness will most likely require a peer-to-peer conversation
medical devices used ... must be FDA approved or conditionally approved for the intended use

external_dependencies.what: Cardiac resynchronization devices out of scope
external_dependencies.quote: Use of external defibrillators and cardiac resynchronization devices is not addressed in this document.

definitions_that_change_meaning.definition_quote: Maximum tolerated doses of appropriately titrated medication (to include beta blockers, ACE inhibitors or ARBs, aldosterone antagonists and diuretics in patients with left ventricular dysfunction).
Ventricular tachycardia that persists for at least 30 seconds or requiring termination due to hemodynamic instability.
Left ventricular dysfunction (LVEF < 50%), prior myocardial infarction, moderate or severe valvular heart disease or complex congenital heart disease.

Class II. Individuals with cardiac disease resulting in slight limitation of physical activity ... ordinary physical activity, (e.g., moderate physical exertion, such as carrying shopping bags up several flights of stairs) results in fatigue, palpitation, dyspnea, or anginal pain.

extraction_hazards: Cover page and header carry tracked-change markup ('Blue underline = insertion, Red strikethrough = deletion'): dates print as '11/1710/20/2024' and '04/15/2024 01/23/2024', merging a deleted and an inserted date.

Revision markup in the criteria themselves may have been flattened: the S-ICD age bullet 'Subcutaneous device is preferred due to younger age of patient Individual is <= 21 years of age' appears to fuse a deleted and an inserted phrase from the redline (inference; the History says the age was replaced by 'younger' on 04/15/2024).
Bullet glyphs are private-use characters; sub-bullets use 'o'; nesting carries the logic.
The 'General Clinical Guideline' (pp. 4-5) is boilerplate shared by every Carelon guideline and contains words like 'repeat', 'peer-to-peer', 'net benefit' that look like criteria.
Code table includes an anesthesia code (00534) and HCPCS device codes (C1721 ...) that are claim codes, not procedures a chart orders.
Page footer 'Carelon Medical Benefits Management' repeated and page numbers within lists.
interesting_structures: Vendor 'Appropriate Use Criteria' with explicit framework, peer-to-peer fallback, and repeat-intervention rules shared across all Carelon guidelines.
Text nearly identical to BCBSM's inclusion list but with <= and >= comparators and no softeners.
Genetic cardiomyopathies (phospholamban, FLNC, lamin A/C) with sex as a criterion item.
Replacement: second branch needs another reason to open the pocket plus proximity to end-of-life.
Substernal codes present but no substernal criteria (gap).
Revision history table lists expansions (LV aneurysm, LGE; genetic cardiomyopathies; replacement).

fit_to_tree.scale: 1 = clean, 5 = needs new constructs or human judgment
fit_to_tree.why: A wide any-of with deterministic numeric leaves is easy; strain is the global one-year survival gate, many diagnoses defined by outside classifications, the tracked-changes damage in the S-ICD age bullet, and absence of a substernal criteria block despite listed codes.
